ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (المر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (١))
His saying, Exalted is He: (المر): its ruling has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara.
(تِلْكَ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ» its khabar (predicate); or it may be the khabar of (المر), with «آيَاتُ» a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
(وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is in the position of the nominative (as a mubtadaʾ), and «الْحَقُّ» is its khabar.
It may also be that the khabar is «مِنْ رَبِّكَ», and «الْحَقُّ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or it is a khabar after a khabar, or the two together are a single khabar. If «الْحَقِّ» had been read in the genitive, it would have been permissible, as an adjective (ṣifa) of «رَبِّكَ». The second view: that «وَالَّذِي» is an adjective of «الْكِتَابِ», the wāw having been brought into the adjective as it was brought in with «التَّائِبِينَ» and «الطَّيِّبِينَ».
And (الْحَقُّ), in the nominative, is on this view the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ (٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "free of pillars".
And al-ʿamad, with fatḥa, is the plural of ʿimād or ʿamūd ("pillar"), like أَدِيمٌ and أَدَمٌ, أَفِيقٌ and أَفَقٌ, إِهَابٌ and أَهَبٌ; and there is no fifth to them.
It is also read with two ḍammas (عُمُدٍ), and it is like كِتَابٌ and كُتُبٌ, رَسُولٌ and رُسُلٌ.
(تَرَوْنَهَا): the object pronoun refers back to the pillars; so «تَرَوْنَهَا» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa).
It may also refer back to the heavens; it is then a ḥāl from them.
(يُدَبِّرُ) and (يُفَصِّلُ): both are read with yāʾ and with nūn; their meaning is clear, and they are both resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
It may also be that the first is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «سَخَّرَ», and the second a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُدَبِّرُ».

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْهَارًا وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ): there are three views on it:
The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the second «جَعَلَ», the implied form being "and He made in it two of a pair from all the fruits". The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثْنَيْنِ», being originally an adjective (ṣifa) of it. The third: that it is attached to the first «جَعَلَ», and the second «جَعَلَ» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ): it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the name of Allah in whichever of the verbs before it this is valid for, namely: رَفَعَ, سَخَّرَ, يُدَبِّرُ, يُفَصِّلُ, مَدَّ and جَعَلَ.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجَاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ يُسْقَى بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ): the majority read it with the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) or as the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase. Al-Ḥasan read «قِطَعًا مُتَجَاوِرَاتٍ», on the implied form "and He made in the earth…".
And (وَجَنَّاتٌ) is likewise, according to the difference (of readings). None of them read «وَزَرْعًا» in the accusative; but some people read it in the nominative, conjoined to «قِطَعٌ», and likewise what follows it; and others read it in the genitive, conjoined to «أَعْنَابٍ». Some people declared this reading weak, because crops are not part of gardens.
Others said: there may be crops in a garden, but between the palms and the vines. It is also said: the implied form is "and plants of crops", so it was conjoined according to the meaning.
And al-ṣinwān is the plural of ṣinw, like قِنْوٌ and قِنْوَانٌ; its plural of paucity is أَصْنَاءٌ. There are two dialectal forms of it: kasra on the ṣād and ḍamma on it, and it has been read with both.
(تُسْقَى): the majority read it with tāʾ, the feminine being for the preceding plural. It is also read with yāʾ (يُسْقَى), i.e. "that is watered".
(نُفَضِّلُ): it is read with nūn and with yāʾ, naming the agent (active); and with yāʾ and fatḥa on the ḍād (يُفَضَّلُ), with «بَعْضُهَا» in the nominative; and that is clear.
(فِي الْأُكُلِ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «نُفَضِّلُ»; or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَعْضَهَا», i.e. "We prefer some of them as something eaten", or "with eating in it".

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَئِذَا كُنَّا تُرَابًا أَئِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٥))
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ): «قَوْلُهُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عَجَبٌ» is a fronted khabar (predicate).
It is also said: «الْعَجَبُ» here means "something astonishing"; on this view «قَوْلُهُمْ» may be nominative by it (as its agent).
(أَئِذَا كُنَّا): the whole statement is in the position of the accusative by «قَوْلُهُمْ». What governs «إِذَا» is a verb that the speech points to, its implied form being "when we are dust, shall we be resurrected?"; and His saying (لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ) points to it. It may not be accusative by «كُنَّا», because «إِذَا» is in a genitive construct with it; nor by «جَدِيدٍ», because what comes after «إِنَّ» does not govern what comes before it.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ»; or it may be an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السَّيِّئَةِ».
And (الْمَثُلَاتُ) is with fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ; its singular is likewise (مَثُلَةٌ).
It is read with sukūn on the tāʾ (الْمَثْلَاتُ); there are two explanations of it. The first: that it is lightened from the plural with ḍamma, fleeing the heaviness of the ḍamma together with the succession of vowels. The second: that the singular was lightened and then the plural was formed on that.
[Translator's note: "the tāʾ" is as written in the source; the letter concerned is the thāʾ.]
It is also read with two ḍammas (الْمُثُلَاتُ), and with ḍamma on the first and sukūn on the second (الْمُثْلَاتُ); ḍamma on the mīm is a dialectal form of it. As for ḍamma on the thāʾ, it may be a dialectal form in the singular, or it may be vowel harmony (itbāʿ) in the plural; and as for sukūn on it, it is according to the two views.
(عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ): a ḥāl from «النَّاسِ», and what governs it is «مَغْفِرَةٍ».
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (٧)).
[Translator's note: the source repeats the text of verse 6 here under the number (٧); the comment that follows concerns verse 7: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ): there are three views on it. The first: that it is a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa), i.e. "and for every people there is a guiding prophet". The second: that the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "and He is, for every people, a guide". The third: its implied form is "you are only a warner, and a guide for every people"; in this there is a separation between the conjunction and the maʿṭūf (conjoined), and they have cited a fair amount of it.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثَى وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا تَحْمِلُ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), and its position is accusative by «يَعْلَمُ».
The second: it is interrogative; it is then accusative by «تَحْمِلُ», and the clause is in the position of the accusative.
And likewise: «وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ».
(وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ): «عِنْدَهُ» may be in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of «شَيْءٍ», or in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «كُلُّ»; what governs it on both views is omitted; and the khabar (predicate) of «كُلُّ» is «بِمِقْدَارٍ».
It may also be an adjective of «مِقْدَارٍ», or an adverb (ẓarf) of what the preposition (in «بِمِقْدَارٍ») is attached to.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with «الْكَبِيرُ» its khabar.
The better practice is to pause on «الْمُتَعَالِ» without yāʾ, because it is the end of a verse; were it not for that, the better practice would be to keep it.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَالٍ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ): its singular is «مُعَقِّبَةٌ», the hāʾ in it being for intensiveness, like «نَسَّابَةٌ» ("a great genealogist"), i.e. "an angel who follows in succession".
It is also said: «مُعَقِّبَةٌ» is an adjective of a group, and then it was put in the plural on that basis.
(مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «مُعَقِّبَاتٌ»; or an adverb (ẓarf); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun that is in it; on this view the speech is complete at it.
It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَحْفَظُونَهُ», i.e. "followers who guard him from before him and from behind him".
And «يَحْفَظُونَهُ» may be an adjective of «مُعَقِّبَاتٌ», or a ḥāl from what the adverbial phrase is attached to.
(مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ): i.e. from the jinn and mankind; so «مِنْ» has its usual meaning. It is also said: «مِنْ» means the bāʾ, i.e. "by the command of Allah". It is also said: it means «عَنْ».
(وَإِذَا أَرَادَ): what governs «إِذَا» is what the answer points to, i.e. "it is not repelled", or "it befalls".
(مِنْ وَالٍ): it is read with imāla (inclining the vowel towards i) because of the kasra; and there is no impediment here.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
And (السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ) has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّوَاعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ): it is said: it is an angel; on this view it has been named with the maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said: thunder is its voice; the implied form on this view is "the possessor of the thunder" or "the thunderer".
And (بِحَمْدِهِ) has been mentioned in al-Baqara in the story of Ādam, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
And (الْمِحَالِ) is of the pattern fiʿāl from al-maḥl, which is strength; one says مَحَلَ بِهِ when he overpowered him. There is another dialectal form of it: with fatḥa on the mīm.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْمَاءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ وَمَا دُعَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ): there are two opinions on it. The first: it is an allusion to the idols, i.e. "and the idols, which call the polytheists to worship them, «لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ»"; He gave them the plural of rational beings according to their belief about them. The second: that they are the polytheists, the implied form being "and the polytheists who call upon the idols besides Allah — they (the idols) do not respond to them", i.e. do not answer them; that is, the idols do not answer them with anything.
(إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ): the implied form is "except a response like the response to one who stretches out his palms". The maṣdar (verbal noun) in this implied form is in a genitive construct with its object, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ). The agent of this maṣdar is implied (muḍmar), and it is the pronoun of the water, i.e. "they do not answer them except as the water answers one who stretches out his palms to it"; and the answering here is an allusion to compliance.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ), the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «بَاسِطِ», and the agent is the pronoun of the water, i.e. "so that the water may reach his mouth".
And (مَا هُوَ): i.e. the water. It may not be the pronoun of the one stretching out, with the agent of «بَالِغ» implied, because when an active participle is predicated of someone other than the one to whom it belongs, the agent must be made overt; on this view it would have been necessary to say "وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ الْمَاءَ". But if you make the hāʾ in «بَالِغِهِ» the pronoun of the water, then «هُوَ» may be the pronoun of the one stretching out.
As for the kāf in «كَبَاسِطِ»: if you make it a particle, there is in it (in what it attaches to) a pronoun referring back to the omitted thing qualified; and if you make it a noun, there is no pronoun in it.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَظِلَالُهُمْ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (ظِلَالُهُمْ) is conjoined to «مَنْ».
And (بِالْغُدُوِّ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَسْجُدُ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي):
it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and its parallels have preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رَابِيًا وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغَاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ وَالْبَاطِلَ فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَاءً وَأَمَّا مَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْدِيَةٌ): it is the plural of وَادٍ ("valley"); the plural of fāʿil on the pattern afʿila is irregular (shādhdh), and we have not heard it in any word other than this one. Its explanation is that fāʿil has come with the meaning of faʿīl; and just as faʿīl has come with (a plural) afʿila, as in جَرِيبٌ and أَجْرِبَةٌ, so has fāʿil.
(بِقَدَرِهَا): an adjective (ṣifa) of «أَوْدِيَةٌ».
(وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ): with yāʾ and with tāʾ.
(عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُوقِدُونَ».
And (ابْتِغَاءَ) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).
(أَوْ مَتَاعٍ): conjoined to «حِلْيَةٍ»; «زَبَدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِثْلُهُ» is an adjective of it, and the khabar (predicate) is «مِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ».
The meaning is: "and among the minerals of the earth, such as copper, there is that which has a scum — namely its dross — like it", i.e. like the foam that is on the water.
And (جُفَاءً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); its hamza is converted from a wāw. It is also said: it is original.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنَى وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لَافْتَدَوْا بِهِ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْحِسَابِ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (١٨)).
(لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا): resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and it is the khabar (predicate) of «الْحُسْنَى».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَنْقُضُونَ الْمِيثَاقَ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ): it may be accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بَابٍ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ): it is a badal (substitute) from «عُقْبَى»; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «يَدْخُلُونَهَا» the khabar (predicate).
And (وَمَنْ صَلَحَ) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the agent pronoun; this was allowed even though it was not emphasised, because the object pronoun has become a separator like the emphasis (tawkīd).
It may also be accusative with the meaning of «مَعَ» ("with").

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَلَامٌ): i.e. "they say: peace".
(بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ): the bāʾ may not be attached to «سَلَامٌ», because of the separation by the khabar (predicate) that this would involve; it is attached only to «عَلَيْكُمْ», or to what that is attached to.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the implied form is "in comparison with the Hereafter".
It may not be an adverb (ẓarf), either of «الْحَيَاةُ» or of «الدُّنْيَا», because they do not occur in the Hereafter; rather it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the implied form is "and the near life, being set beside the Hereafter, is not…".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "tranquillity by it", i.e. tranquillity comes about for them through the remembrance of Allah.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْقُلُوبُ», i.e. "they are at rest, with the remembrance of Allah in them".

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (طُوبَى لَهُمْ) is a second mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of the first.
It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who believed"; then «طُوبَى لَهُمْ» is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and what governs it is «آمَنُوا» and «عَمِلُوا».
It may also be that «الَّذِينَ» is a badal (substitute) from (مَنْ أَنَابَ), or (accusative) by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean").
It may also be that «طُوبَى» is in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "He made (جَعَلَ)…".
Its wāw is a replacement for a yāʾ, because it is from al-ṭīb ("goodness"); it was replaced by a wāw because of the ḍamma before it.
And (حُسْنُ مَآبٍ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the nūn and the genitive construct; it is conjoined to «طُوبَى» if you make it a mubtadaʾ.
It was also read with fatḥa on the nūn and the genitive construct (وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ); it is conjoined to «طُوبَى» on the view that it is accusative.
It is read irregularly with fatḥa on the nūn and the nominative of «مَآبٌ» (وَحُسْنَ مَآبٌ); «حَسُنَ» on this view is a verb, the ḍamma of whose sīn was transferred to the ḥāʾ; and this is permissible in faʿula when it is for praise or blame.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهَا أُمَمٌ لِتَتْلُوَ عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمَنِ قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتَابِ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): the implied form is "the matter is as We have informed you".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَى بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعًا أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ لَوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَا يَزَالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهُمْ بِمَا صَنَعُوا قَارِعَةٌ أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا مِنْ دَارِهِمْ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآنًا): the answer of «لَوْ» is omitted, i.e. "it would have been this Qurʾān".
Al-Farrāʾ said: its answer is placed before it, i.e. "and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, even if there were a Qurʾān…", by way of hyperbole.
(أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَى): the reason for dropping the tāʾ from this verb while keeping it in the two verbs before it is that «الْمَوْتَى» includes the real masculine, and gives it predominance (taghlīb); so dropping the tāʾ was better; while «الْجِبَالُ» and «الْأَرْضُ» are not like that.
(أَنْ لَوْ يَشَاءُ): in the position of the accusative by «يَيْأَسْ», because its meaning is "has it not become clear (to them) and do they not know?".
(أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا): the agent (fāʿil) of «تَحُلُّ» is the pronoun of «الْقَارِعَةُ». It is also said: it is for the second person, i.e. "or you, O Muḥammad, alight near them with the punishment"; then the position of the clause is accusative, conjoined to «تُصِيبُ».

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَى كُلِ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ بِظَاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بَلْ زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَكْرُهُمْ وَصُدُّوا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ): it is conjoined to «كَسَبَتْ», i.e. "and for their setting up partners". It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(وَصُدُّوا): it is read with fatḥa on the ṣād (وَصَدُّوا), i.e. "and they turned others away"; with ḍamma on it, i.e. "and Satan, or their partners, turned them away"; and with kasra on it (وَصِدُّوا), its original being صُدِدُوا with ḍamma on the first letter; the kasra of the dāl was transferred to the ṣād.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ وَظِلُّهَا تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَعُقْبَى الْكَافِرِينَ النَّارُ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "and among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden". On this view (تَجْرِي) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) in «وُعِدَ», i.e. "they were promised it, the flowing of its rivers being foreordained".
Al-Farrāʾ said: the khabar is «تَجْرِي». According to the Basrans this is an error, because rivers do not flow beneath the description; that is only an attribute of the muḍāf ilayhi. His (al-Farrāʾ's) ground is that «الْمَثَلُ» here means "the description", so it is like your saying "Zayd's description is that he is tall".
It may also be that «تَجْرِي» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ): it is like (تَجْرِي) on the two views.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَنْقُصُهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun, or from «الْأَرْضَ».

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ): it is read in the singular (الْكَافِرُ), it being a generic noun (jins), and in the plural, according to the original.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ): it is read with fatḥa on the mīm; it means «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), and concerning its position there are two views. The first: it is nominative, following the position of the name of Allah, i.e. "Allah suffices, and the one who has… suffices". The second: it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the wording of the name of Allah the Exalted. On this view «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ» is nominative by the adverbial phrase, because it relies on (something before it) by being a ṣila (relative clause).
It may also be a khabar (predicate), the mubtadaʾ (subject) being «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ».
It is also read «وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ», with kasra on the mīm, as a particle (preposition); on this view «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ» is a mubtadaʾ, or the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase.
It is also read «عُلِمَ الْكِتَابُ», as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), and it is what governs «مِنْ».
